items.h: Green Line shuts down across downtown for Halloween weekend
items.sum: No Green Line trains run between North Station and Kenmore, Babcock Street or Heath Street this weekend, with shuttles and some bus routes at no fare, and the T warns trips may run 25 minutes longer.

items.h: Warm Friday, then a cooler Halloween night for trick-or-treaters
items.sum: Temperatures climb toward 70 on Friday before a cold front brings cooler air, so parents should plan a sweater or light jacket over costumes Saturday night.

items.h: Noah Kahan adds four Fenway Park shows for 2027
items.sum: The singer-songwriter returns to Fenway Park for concerts on May 29, May 30, June 1 and June 2.

items.h: Somerville looks to save arts spaces with a cultural trust
items.sum: The city is proposing a trust that could buy and preserve venues for artists and performers.

items.h: Mass. Lottery tries scented scratch tickets for the holidays
items.sum: The lottery's first scented holiday tickets aim to give sagging scratch sales a lift.

items.h: Health Connector open enrollment is underway
items.sum: Residents who buy coverage through the Massachusetts Health Connector can sign up or switch plans during open enrollment, which runs into January 2027.

items.h: About 70,000 Massachusetts residents see medical debt wiped away
items.sum: A foundation and a nonprofit teamed up to erase roughly $38 million in medical debt for residents across the state.

items.h: Harvard Book Store opening a second shop in downtown Boston
items.sum: The Cambridge bookseller is bringing a new Union Street location with a cafe and a children's area this fall.

items.h: Bostonhenge sunset lines up with Back Bay streets this week
items.sum: The twice-a-year moment when the setting sun aligns with Back Bay buildings is back, with tips on where and when to watch.

items.h: Hello, Old Friend brings Detroit-style pizza to West Roxbury
items.sum: The pizza maker known for pop-ups and a Roslindale residency is opening its own West Roxbury location.

items.h: Wu proposes faster path for new neighborhood restaurants
items.sum: The plan would let existing permits move to new owners without a fresh review in some takeout cases, cutting waits from about four months to under two weeks, pending licensing board and City Council approval.

items.h: Hasbro's CEO talks about the toymaker's move to the Seaport
items.sum: After more than a century in Rhode Island, Hasbro is relocating its headquarters to Boston's Seaport, and its chief executive explains why.

items.h: Fields Corner Post Office will stay open after all
items.sum: A lease extension reversed a planned closing, keeping the Dorchester post office serving the neighborhood.

items.h: Nikki Giovanni's archives open to the public at Boston University
items.sum: BU's Howard Gotlieb center now holds the papers of the celebrated poet.

items.h: Voice of Logan contest narrowed to eight finalists
items.sum: Massport's search for a new announcement voice at Logan Airport came down to eight finalists, with public voting closing Wednesday night.

items.h: State mails letters to help residents claim lost money
items.sum: The treasurer's office is testing a new approach that contacts people directly about unclaimed property instead of relying on an online search.

items.h: Red Line to pick up speed between JFK/UMass and North Quincy
items.sum: The MBTA plans to raise train speeds to 50 mph on that stretch of the Braintree branch.

items.h: Fallen leaves caused an hours-long Commuter Rail delay
items.sum: The T says slippery leaves on the tracks were behind a lengthy disruption for Commuter Rail riders.

items.h: Galvin urges voters to cast ballots early
items.sum: The secretary of state expects a slower Election Day and encourages voters to use early voting.

items.h: High-end Japanese restaurant group from a James Beard winner heading to Boston
items.sum: An acclaimed chef's upscale Japanese restaurant chain is expanding into the Boston market.

items.h: Popular sub shop chain closes its Downtown Crossing spot
items.sum: A well-known sandwich chain has shut its location in Downtown Crossing.

items.h: Saus is leaving Somerville's Bow Market
items.sum: The Bow Market eatery says it is time to move on and is closing its Somerville spot.

items.h: Attleboro's Stone-E-Lea Golf Course to close after 70-plus years
items.sum: The family-run course will close at the end of the season and is listed for sale for possible redevelopment.

items.h: mRNA cancer vaccine cuts melanoma recurrence in study
items.sum: Cambridge-based Moderna and partner Merck report their vaccine lowered the chance of melanoma returning.

items.h: MWRA picks MassDOT highway chief Gulliver as its new leader
items.sum: Jonathan Gulliver will run the agency that provides water and sewer service to about 3.1 million people.

items.h: Glass shards turn up on a Swampscott school field
items.sum: Town officials are dealing with what they call an odd problem of glass contaminating a school athletic field.

items.h: Brigham nurses vote down tentative contract
items.sum: Nurses at Brigham and Women's Hospital rejected the deal and want to return to bargaining.

items.h: Which Massachusetts ZIP codes made the Wealthy 1000 list
items.sum: The annual national ranking of the richest ZIP codes includes a number of Massachusetts communities.

items.h: Boston opens public comment on its yearly housing and community report
items.sum: The city is taking resident feedback on its annual performance report for federal housing and community development funds.
